name: Civil unrest
summary: French union strikes ran to a 17 Nov national day; Indonesian protests met force on 10 Nov; no deadly nationwide unrest
state: French unions held a second interprofessional strike day on 17 Nov after a 5 Nov day that the interior ministry put at 575,000 people, with tear gas and some clashes but no deaths (Al Jazeera; Connexion). In Indonesia, police detained 157 people in Yogyakarta during anti-government protests on 10 Nov, with injuries reported and no deaths (Human Rights Watch). Significant protests in several countries keep Watch; searches on 21 Nov found no deadly nationwide unrest or major crackdown in a large country.
for_you: Travellers to France may meet transport and service disruption on strike days; check FCDO travel advice. Further strike days and weekend protests tend to follow while pay talks stall.
rubric_hit: Watch: significant protests in several countries (France 17 Nov, Indonesia 10 Nov); no deadly nationwide unrest

sources.title: Al Jazeera — Hundreds of thousands protest across France over high cost of living
Connexion — Strikes and protests in France in November 2026

why: Mass protest and state crackdowns signal political fragility and can topple governments.
drivers: Cost of living, elections, corruption, repression, food and fuel prices.

rubric.alert: Deadly nationwide unrest or a state crackdown in a major country.
rubric.watch: Significant protests in several countries or deadly unrest in one.
rubric.normal: No deadly mass unrest in large countries.
